jon.pryor (Sapphire): Hey team — onboarding question. We're planning to import a customer key into Azure Key Vault (HSM) and wire it to Redwood for envelope encryption. A few quick things we need clarified: required RBAC roles for the SP, recommended audit log retention for compliance, and whether Redwood expects the key to allow wrapKey/unwrapKey only or also sign/verify. Also need to confirm the rotation flow — who initiates data key rewraps and is there any downtime. 

maya (Redwood Support): Thanks Jonathan — welcome! Quick clarifying Qs: are you doing a key import or generating the key inside Key Vault? And are you using a single SP for all regions or per-region SPs?

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Importing a key (we have to bring an existing RSA 2048 HSM-protected key). One SP per env for now (staging/prod), single region eastus for prod.

alex (eng-security): For import into AKV HSM: Redwood needs the SP to have Key Vault Data Plane permissions: wrapKey, unwrapKey, get, list. We do NOT require sign/verify unless you expect Redwood to use the key for signing (we only do envelope wrapping). Recommended role: a custom role with those explicit actions attached to the service principal. Avoid giving 'Key Vault Contributor' if you want least privilege.

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Got it. For audit logging retention — compliance asks for 2 years. Is that feasible? Where do we point logs?

maya (Redwood Support): We ingest KMS audit events for rewraps and key access verification. For Azure we expect you to forward Azure Diagnostic Settings to a customer-managed Log Analytics workspace or Event Hub that we can reference via your private deployment. For Hosted customers we ask for 90 days retention by default; 2 years is fine for Private/Dedicated with an enterprise contract — but you'll need to host the logs in your account and provide a read-only principal.

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Ok makes sense. What's the exact minimum policy for wrap/unwrap? Example snippet would help.

alex (eng-security): Example Azure RBAC JSON (assign to your SP):
```json
{
  "Actions": [
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/deploy/action",
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/wrap/action",
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/unwrap/action",
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/get/action",
    "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/list/action"
  ],
  "NotActions": [],
  "DataActions": [],
  "NotDataActions": []
}
```
Note: in practice create a Key Vault access policy granting wrapKey, unwrapKey, get to the SP object id.

secops-bot: [automated] Example audit event we look for on rewrap: 
- operationName: UnwrapKey
- caller: <svc-principal-id>
- resource: vaults/<vault-name>/keys/<key-name>
- correlationId present

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Good, that answers most. About rotation: will Redwood rotate the customer key or rotate data-encryption keys (DEKs)? Do we need to do anything when we rotate the master key in AKV?

alex (eng-security): Redwood never modifies your KMS master key. Our flow: Redwood generates ephemeral DEKs (data keys) per-tenant, wraps them with your KMS key (WrapKey) and stores the wrapped blob. On rotation: if you create a new key version or rotate the key in AKV, you must trigger a rewrap of DEKs so they are re-encrypted with the new key version. Redwood provides a Rewrap API (or we can run a one-off job in Private deployments) that iterates DEKs and calls Unwrap with the old key and Wrap with the new key. No downtime expected — we perform rewraps online; there may be transient increased latency for first access as we rewrap on-demand if you choose lazy rewrap mode.

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Rewrap API — is that available for Hosted? Anything we need to configure ahead of time?

maya (Redwood Support): For Hosted, we handle rewraps but we require: 1) both key versions to be present and enabled in AKV, 2) the Redwood service principal must have wrap/unwrap on both versions, and 3) you must grant read access to the audit logs for validation. For Private we can run the rewrap job within your VPC; you'll need to schedule a maintenance window only if you want a bulk immediate rewrap (otherwise rolling/lazy is default).

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Last question: envelope format. Do you expect a specific KMS envelope schema? We have an existing app that uses an envelope: {"alg":"RSA-OAEP","ver":1,"wrapped_key":...}.

alex (eng-security): We accept a couple of common envelope formats. For portability use: JSON with keys: version, algo, wrapped_key (base64), key_id (AKV key URI), and optional metadata (key_version, created_at). Example accepted minimal envelope: 
```json
{"version":"1","algo":"RSA-OAEP","wrapped_key":"<base64>","key_uri":"https://myvault.vault.azure.net/keys/keyname/abcd"}
```
If your current schema maps to those fields we can ingest as-is. If not, share a sample and we can confirm.

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Perfect — I'll paste a sample in a follow-up. One last operational check: during key import to AKV, any recommended validation steps to avoid access issues?

maya (Redwood Support): Do these validations: 
- Ensure key is enabled and not expired
- Test wrap/unwrap from a separate client using the SP credentials (az keyvault key wrap --algorithm RSA-OAEP)
- Confirm Key Vault network rules allow Redwood (for Private, make sure VNet/private endpoint is configured)
- Provide the SP object id to Redwood so we can verify permissions ahead of time

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Great — thanks. I'll run the tests and share the sample envelope + az commands.

alex (eng-security): If you want us to do a quick permission sanity check once you share the SP id and sample envelope, we can run the verification script and confirm everything looks good.

jon.pryor (Sapphire): Appreciate it, will send later today. :thumbsup:
